cover.title: McKinley Help
cover.subtitle: Report a repair in a short chat, any time of day.

steps.say: Meet McKinley Help, an AI chat assistant that helps you take care of your apartment, any time of day.
When something breaks at home, getting it fixed usually starts with a phone call.
You call the office, wait on hold, or leave a voicemail, and hope every detail gets written down. After hours, it's even harder.
McKinley Help replaces that call with a short chat. You describe the problem in your own words, and it builds a complete repair request for you.
It also helps people looking for a new home, with questions about our communities and tour requests.
To start, open the assistant on your phone or computer, and sign in to your account.
It greets you by name and offers shortcuts for the most common tasks: report a repair, check your requests, ask about your renewal, or talk to the office.
You can tap a shortcut, or just type what's going on, the way you'd explain it to a neighbor.

do.type: My AC stopped cooling again. This is the third time this year.

steps.say: Then press Send.
If anything is missing, the assistant asks a short follow-up question. Here, it needs to know which room the problem is in.
Under the reply, a progress note shows what's still needed to finish the request.
Marisol answers in one line, and adds that maintenance may come in while she's out.

do.type: The living room. You can come in if I'm not home.

steps.say: Now the assistant shows a repair request card, filled in from the conversation. Ready to send means nothing is missing.
Read it row by row: what's wrong, where it is, and whether maintenance may enter.
It also adds useful history from your account. Here, an earlier AC request is still open, so the team can see this is a repeat problem.
Nothing is sent until you say so. If a detail is wrong, just type the correction, or tap Don't send.
When everything looks right, tap Send repair request.
You get a reference number right away, so you can mention it later.
To see where it stands, tap Check its status, or come back any time and ask.
The reply lists every request on your account, each with a clear status, like Follow-up owed, or Saved.
If you'd rather speak with someone, tap Talk to a person. The assistant prepares a note for the office with what you've already said, so you don't have to repeat yourself.
Tap Send note, and it's on its way to the team.
Some problems can't wait. If something is dangerous, like a gas smell, just say so.

do.type: I smell gas in my kitchen

steps.say: The assistant puts safety first. It tells you to leave right away, and to call nine one one once you're outside, before anything else.

do.hover: Leave now, then call 911 from outside

steps.caption: The assistant puts safety first. It tells you to leave right away, and to call 911 once you're outside, before anything else.

steps.say: It also saves an urgent note for the team, but calling nine one one yourself always comes first.
steps.caption: It also saves an urgent note for the team, but calling 911 yourself always comes first.

steps.say: On the McKinley side, requests land in the staff queue, with urgent issues at the top.
Each one shows the problem, the room, the entry permission and the priority, so a team member can review it and plan the visit.
Good to know: the assistant isn't linked to McKinley's maintenance system yet, so it can't book a visit time for you. A team member takes it from there.

do.hover: Nothing here reaches a real system

steps.say: So whenever something needs fixing, open the chat, describe the problem, check your request, and send. Thanks for watching.
